ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A closed circular loop of radius $r$ with resistance $R$ and electromotive force $\mathcal{E}$ is coaxial with a long, thin air-core solenoid of length $\ell$ ($\ell \gg r$), cross-sectional area $A$ ($\sqrt{A} \ll r$), and $N$ turns. The solenoid carries a constant current $I$. The currents in the solenoid and loop are in the same direction (clockwise in the figure).

1. Find the force $F_1$ acting on the solenoid when its head $O_1$ is positioned at the center $O$ of the loop. What is the force $F_2$ acting on the solenoid when its tail $O_2$ is located at the center of the loop?

The solenoid carries a constant current $I$. The currents in the solenoid and loop are in the same direction (clockwise in the figure). 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a slender solenoid placed along the horizontal z axis, with the right end labeled O1, the left end labeled O2, the solenoid length labeled ℓ, the number of turns labeled N, and with current I. On the right side there is a large circular closed loop with radius labeled r; the loop is coaxial with the solenoid, the center of the circle is labeled O, and the z axis passes through the center of the circle and points to the right. A power supply is drawn below the loop, labeled with electromotive force ℰ and positive and negative terminals; in the situation shown, the right end O1 of the solenoid is located near the center of the loop, while O2 is far away on the left. Reasoning: The loop resistance is R and the electromotive force is ℰ, so the loop current is i=ℰ/R. Since the solenoid cross section is very small, the external magnetic field experienced by each turn can be approximately taken as the magnetic field of the circular loop on the axis. The magnetic field of the circular loop at a distance z from the center on the axis is B_loop(z), where at the center B_loop(0)=μ0 i/(2r), and because ℓ≫r, B_loop(±ℓ)≈0. Use mutual inductance to express the interaction. Let the number of turns per unit length of the solenoid be N/ℓ, then the total magnetic flux of the circular-loop magnetic field passing through all turns of the solenoid gives the mutual inductance M=(N/ℓ)(A/i)∫_{tail}^{head} B_loop(z) dz. When the solenoid translates along the +z direction, under the condition of constant currents, the axial force acting on the solenoid is F=I i dM/dx. First case: the head end O1 is at the center O of the circular ring. Take tail=-ℓ, head=0, then dM/dx=(N A/(ℓ i))[B_loop(0)-B_loop(-ℓ)]≈(N A/(ℓ i))B_loop(0). Therefore F1=I i dM/dx≈I i (N A/(ℓ i)) μ0 i/(2r)=μ0 N I A i/(2ℓ r). Substituting i=ℰ/R gives F1=μ0 N I A ℰ/(2ℓ R r). According to the same-direction current and +z direction convention shown in the figure, this is a positive sign. Second case: the tail end O2 is at the center O of the circular ring. Take tail=0, head=ℓ, then dM/dx=(N A/(ℓ i))[B_loop(ℓ)-B_loop(0)]≈-(N A/(ℓ i))B_loop(0). Therefore F2=I i dM/dx=-μ0 N I A ℰ/(2ℓ R r)=-F1.
